transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-16 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: All-hands (virtual)
Attendees: Aisha, Samir, Melissa, Diego, Priya, Jon, Lena + companywide listen-in

Auto-summary (auto-gen): holiday readiness check, deployment freeze plan, targeted rollouts, action owners assigned.

00:00 Aisha Tan: ok everyone, thanks for being punctual, I want to keep this tight — about an hour. we have the usual holiday event coming up and we need to make sure customers are covered and we don't surprise anyone with a deployment while half the org is out.

00:22 Samir Rao: yep, I'll start with product perspective. we've been getting a few requests for last-minute model bumps from pilot customers, and we have to decide on a gate for those. do we allow model rollouts during the freeze if they pass a shadow test?

00:45 Melissa Chen: uh, my strong preference is no wide rollouts, like no mass traffic migrations. small canaries with SE oversight, and only if infra signs off. we saw last year — remember the K-V cash warming issue? lead to longer tails.

01:08 Diego Alvarez: side note, last year's K-V cash — that was an S3 warmup mismatch, people call it K-V cash in the notes — anyway, ops can support a small set of canaries. but we need explicit exemption process.

01:30 Priya Kapoor: capacity in EU is our main risk. dedicated pools are near predictable but holiday traffic patterns change. i'd like to propose a smoke test on 12-20 to validate autoscale and our routing fallback.

02:02 Jon Park: can we make that smoke test a standard script? automatable so it's not a one-off? we should capture token latencies and cold-starts. also, include a path that triggers fallback to a cheaper variant so customers see graceful degradation.

02:30 Lena Morris: for security, pagers must stay strict. even if we reduce on-call headcount, thresholds should be tuned to avoid noise — escalate only meaningful incidents. SOC2 audit lag means we can't drop anything.

03:05 Aisha Tan: exact. so proposal: deployment freeze from 2026-12-23 00:00 UTC through 2026-12-27 23:59 UTC. exemptions: security patches, emergency infra fixes, and approved model hotfixes with product and infra signoff. agree?

03:30 Melissa Chen: agree with that window. also recommend a 'soft freeze' period 12-21 to 12-22 where only low-risk pushes allowed, just to clear queued small fixes.

03:55 Samir Rao: +1 to soft freeze. also, add an owner to approve exceptions — maybe Samir + Priya can jointly approve, and they record approvals in the freeze tracker.

04:20 Diego Alvarez: ops will need a rota. I propose on-call rotas: primary coverage by Diego, then two senior on-call engineers rotating through short shifts. we will publish a public-facing status page message that lists support hours and expected response times.

04:43 Jon Park: public-facing messaging needs a short version and a detailed FAQ. the short version for customers in the actual status page header and the FAQ for enterprise accounts. I'll draft both.

05:15 Lena Morris: don't forget the compliance angle — for enterprise customers with strict data residency we must note that any emergency fallback to other regions requires consent. Priya, does KMS/HSM change anything for planned failovers?

05:40 Priya Kapoor: if we failover between regions, keys must be available; for some customers keys are region-bound. we need to compile the list of customers with region-bound KMS and add them to the exemption list to prevent unplanned failovers.

06:05 Aisha Tan: good catch. Jon — can you coordinate with solutions and account teams to get that list?

06:20 Jon Park: yes, I'll ping AE and CSM leads after this.

06:35 (laughter/overlap)

07:00 Melissa Chen: ops note — let's also lock down autoscaling config for dedicated pools and avoid changing kernel selection or quantization configs during freeze. those are lower-level but can cause perf shifts.

07:28 Samir Rao: speaking of kernel selection, is anyone seeing regressions with the new kernel from the runtime team? last patch seemed to have a small perf delta on long sequences. we should avoid exposing that change during holiday.

07:55 Melissa Chen: we can hold the kernel updates until after the freeze unless there's a critical patch. hold on, I want to confirm with runtime before finalizing.

08:10 Aisha Tan: operationally sound. Diego, runbook status? are playbooks up to date?

08:20 Diego Alvarez: runbooks are 80% updated. main missing bits are recently added dedicated routing policies and the EU smoke test steps. I'll own completion by Dec 17.

08:40 Aisha Tan: ok that fits the timeline. next: customer comms — how transparent are we? do we tell customers about the exact freeze dates and the exception process?

09:05 Jon Park: yes we should. short banner on status page plus direct emails to enterprise accounts explaining SLA impact and emergency contact. also include 'how to request an exception' flow.

09:28 Priya Kapoor: add note that HSM/KMS-bound keys won't be moved; for those customers we'll offer dedicated handling.

09:45 Lena Morris: in the event of security incident, exemption applies automatically for patches. but we must send a follow-up report post-incident.

10:05 (pause)

10:20 Samir Rao: timeline recap — smoke test on 12-20, freeze 12-23 to 12-27, post-freeze stabilization through 12-30. owners: Priya for capacity, Diego for runbooks, Jon for comms, Melissa for merge freeze enforcement.

10:50 Aisha Tan: can we get a quick read on staffing? who's definitely OOO and minimal coverage?

11:10 Melissa Chen: infra team will have skeleton crew: Melissa, Priya, two infra SREs. runtime team will have a single lead on call. engineering will triage.

11:30 Diego Alvarez: operations will vendor-support the hotline 24/7 with on-call escalations. but we need to keep paging sane — Lena, can you propose new page thresholds?

11:50 Lena Morris: yes, I'll propose adjusted thresholds focused on error-budget burn and latency SLO breaches, not single request errors. will share by 12-18.

12:12 Jon Park: question from chat — will Dedicated customers see stricter SLAs during the freeze?

12:25 Priya Kapoor: no, SLAs stand. we just limit changes. routing fallback policy keeps availability target but may route to different model variants under capacity stress; we'll document that.

12:50 Samir Rao: mention competition — some customers asked about vendor options if they need continuous rollout windows. we should be clear where we stand: we prioritize stability during holidays, and we offer scheduled maintenance windows if they need frequent rapid iteration.

13:15 Aisha Tan: ok let's finalize decisions now. deployment freeze 12-23 through 12-27 with a soft freeze 12-21 to 12-22. exemptions require Samir+Priya approval and a public tracker entry. EU smoke test 12-20. publish comms 12-17.

13:50 (brief cross talk)

14:10 Diego Alvarez: final question about monitoring dashboards — do we add a special 'holiday view' that surfaces only high-priority alerts?

14:30 Melissa Chen: yes, we can create a holiday dashboard with reduced noise and critical KPIs: p50/p95 latency, token throughput, error rate, model fallback counts. I'll own the dashboard and handoff to ops.

14:55 Aisha Tan: wrap up — thanks everyone. please treat the action items as high priority; we'll run a 15-min follow-up on 12-18 to confirm readiness.

15:10 Samir Rao: quick note: Jon will also coordinate with account leads to make sure enterprise customers with special contracts are informed.

15:25 Jon Park: will do.

15:40 (meeting closes)

Recap / Next steps (auto-gen):
- Freeze window approved: 2026-12-23 to 2026-12-27 (soft freeze 12-21 to 12-22).
- Smoke test in EU: 2026-12-20 (owner: Priya + Ops).
- Comms: publish status page banner + enterprise email draft by 2026-12-17 (owner: Jon).
- Runbook and on-call update: Diego by 2026-12-17.
- Pager threshold tuning: Lena by 2026-12-18.
- Dashboard holiday view: Melissa by 2026-12-18.
